key_insight: Self-powered microsystems need not only better energy harvesters, but also system-level co-design of materials, power management, and storage to achieve truly maintenance-free operation.
engineering_relevance: The review is directly relevant to IoT, wearable, and cyber-physical devices because it maps the main pathways to battery-free operation and the integration bottlenecks that determine real-world deployability.
method: Surveyed triboelectric, piezoelectric/pyroelectric, indoor photovoltaic, and RF rectenna harvesting technologies.
Compared hybrid multi-source integration strategies for broader ambient-energy capture.
Highlighted power-management and storage constraints such as cold-start PMICs, impedance matching, and storage degradation.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites reported advances such as liquid-solid TENGs, nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators that broaden bandwidth by over 300%, and metamaterial RF harvesters, but it does not present a new experimental dataset.
watch_item: Hybrid harvesting systems may underperform in practice if cold-start circuits, impedance matching, and storage aging are not addressed under realistic field conditions.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
